FN-6IQS111-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 278
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/10/2024
Senate Bill 278 as introduced would establish the Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Program to provide injury compensation benefits to full-time public K-12 and
postsecondary education employees in the state. This bill would also provide for compensation
payments, medical benefits, vocational rehabilitation and durable medical equipment, and would
require the payment of two-thirds of an injured employee's salary if placed in a temporary or
permanent disability status.
Additionally, this bill would create the three-member Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Board to administer the program and oversee the benefits paid to injured
employees. Members of the board shall receive no compensation but would be reimbursed for
travel and per diem expenses paid from the fund at the same rate as state employees.
Further, this bill would establish the non-reverting Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Trust Fund, to pay claims, benefits, administrative costs, and all other costs of
the program and further provisions that any unspent or unencumbered funds shall be carried
over to the next fiscal year. Monies in the Fund may be invested and reinvested by the Director
of Finance, through the Division of Risk Management.
Based on information provided by privately contracted workers compensation consultants, the
cost of this program to provide coverage for full-time public K-12 and postsecondary employees
would be an estimated minimum of $15.6 million.

FN-6IQS111-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 278
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 05/02/2024
Senate Bill 278 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would establish
the Public Education Employee Injury Compensation Program to provide injury compensation
benefits to full-time public K-12 education employees in the state beginning no later than
October 1, 2025.
Additionally, this bill would create the five-member Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Board to administer the program and oversee the benefits paid to injured
employees. Members of the board shall receive no compensation but would be reimbursed for
travel and per diem expenses paid from the fund at the same rate as state employees.
Further, this bill would establish the non-reverting Public Education Employee Injury
Compensation Trust Fund in the State Treasury to fund the program.
Based on information provided by privately contracted workers' compensation consultants, the
cost of this program to provide coverage for full-time public K-12 employees would be an
estimated minimum of $14.9 million.
